_pkcs12_decode_safe_contents assumes oid is safe for fixed-literal strcmp dispatch, but it never clears the buffer before bagId parsing or the later attribute read. On the staged witness, bagId bytes 06 01 F7 survive the bag_type gate via GNUTLS_BAG_UNKNOWN, and attribute bytes 06 02 2A F2 are then read into the same oid buffer before the KEY_ID_OID comparison. The saved MSAN trace ties the sink back to the oid stack allocation and reports the first uninitialized byte at offset 4 in the compare window. A correct fix zero-initializes oid before these reads or avoids fixed-literal strcmp on partially initialized storage.

The staged witness preserves the outer DATA_OID authSafe, the first inner pkcs7-data entry, the first SafeBag bagId bytes 06 01 F7, and the first bag-attribute type bytes 06 02 2A F2 for later PKCS#12 decoding.
simple_parse starts its search with idx == 0 and asks for the first bag from the imported PKCS#12 object, making the witness-controlled first AuthenticatedSafe entry reachable.
Decodes the imported outer authSafe into ASN.1 tree c2 representing the inner AuthenticatedSafe sequence from which bag 0 is selected.

After setting root2 to ?1.contentType, get_bag reads the first AuthenticatedSafe member's contentType into oid. Static ASN.1 parsing of the staged PoC shows this OID is pkcs7-data, so the data bag path is selected.

anchors.note: The first entry's contentType matches DATA_OID, so get_bag targets ?1.content and calls _parse_safe_contents on the unencrypted SafeContents payload instead of treating the bag as encrypted.

Extracts the selected ?1.content OCTET STRING into content. These attacker-controlled SafeContents bytes contain the first SafeBag bagId bytes 06 01 F7 and the first bag-attribute type bytes 06 02 2A F2 that later drive the vulnerable dispatch.

Allocates the stack buffer later used for bag-attribute dispatch without initializing it. MemorySanitizer identifies this stack allocation in _pkcs12_decode_safe_contents as the origin of the poisoned bytes consumed at the sink.
Decodes the attacker-controlled SafeContents bytes into ASN.1 tree c2, exposing the first SafeBag's ?1.bagId and ?1.bagAttributes.?1.type entries for the later gates and attribute dispatch.

After setting root to ?1.bagId, the function reads the first SafeBag's bagId into oid. The staged witness encodes those bytes as 06 01 F7; the later oid2bag result shows this read succeeded and yielded an unrecognized bag OID string that is carried forward in oid.

Maps the bagId OID to a bag type and checks the abort gate. oid2bag returns GNUTLS_BAG_UNKNOWN (20) for any unrecognized OID, so this staged bagId survives as bag_type >= 0 and parsing continues into bagValue and bagAttributes instead of aborting.

In the first bagAttributes iteration, the helper reads ?1.bagAttributes.?1.type into the same oid buffer without clearing it first. The staged PoC encodes that attribute type as 06 02 2A F2; combined with the saved MSAN report that bytes from offset 4 are still uninitialized at the following strcmp, this successful helper call leaves oid not fully defined before dispatch.

MSAN sink. KEY_ID_OID is the 21-character literal 1.2.840.113549.1.9.21, so strcmp invokes __interceptor_memcmp on a 22-byte region. Because the first poisoned byte is still at oid[4], the compare reads the uninitialized tail and reports use-of-uninitialized-value.
